'''Ray Bandar''' (1927 - 23 December 2017)<ref name=Yollin-BoneCollector>{{cite news|last1=Yollin|first1=Patricia|title=The Bone Collector|date=2007-01-20|newspaper=San Francisco Chronicle|url=http://www.sfgate.com/bayarea/article/The-Bone-Collector-Ray-Bandar-who-has-2622427.php|access-date=2023-01-16}}</ref><ref name=Cataldo-LifeWithSkulls>{{cite web|last1=Cataldo|first1=Beth|title=Ray Bandar: A Life with Skulls|url=https://bethcataldo.com/portfolio/ray-bandar-a-life-with-skulls/|date=2017-08-17|access-date=2023-01-16}}</ref> was a [[scientist]], [[researcher]], [[teacher]], [[naturalist]], and [[artist]] living in the [[San Francisco]], [[California]] area. He had collected more than 7,000 bone specimens, primarily skulls, from animals across the world, keeping them throughout his home in a collection nicknamed the "Bone Palace".<ref name=Yollin-BoneCollector /> The [[California Academy of Sciences]] legally authorized him to gather specimens under its permits, and inherited his collection after his death.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Wong|first1=Kathleen M.|url=http://research.calacademy.org/calwild/2002spring/stories/skulls.html|title=A Man for All Skulls article on Bandar's work|magazine=California Wild|date=Spring 2002|publisher=California Academy of Sciences|access-date=2023-01-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Dowd|first1=Katie|title=Ray 'Bones' Bandar's collection of 6,000 skulls gets new home in San Francisco|date=2018-03-01|work=SF Gate|url=https://www.sfgate.com/bayarea/article/skulls-bone-palace-sf-collection-database-resource-12720438.php|access-date=2023-01-16}}</ref>

From May–November 2014 the California Academy of Sciences had an exhibit named "Skulls". This exhibit displayed many skulls from the Ray Bandar collection as well as highlighting a bone cleaning technique using flesh eating beetles, and compared bones from various species to learn more about an animals’ history and their evolution and how environmental changes such as pollution and disease have affected them.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gereben|first1=Janos|title=Skulls head nifty Academy of Sciences show|url=http://www.sfexaminer.com/sanfrancisco/skulls-head-nifty-academy-of-sciences-show/Content?oid=2805433|website=San Francisco Examiner|publisher=The San Francisco Examiner|accessdate=November 27, 2014}}</ref>

He was the subject of the 30-minute documentary, "Ray Bandar: A Life With Skulls" (2006) by filmmaker [[Beth Cataldo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sfgate.com/thingstodo/article/REP-PICKS-2598932.php|title=REP PICKS|last=Harmanci|first=Reyhan|date=April 26, 2007|work=SFGate|access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref><ref name=Cataldo-LifeWithSkulls />
